answer: Eccentricity-Weighted Relay Credit. Each agent earns credit only when its messages traverse peers that are topologically distant, measured by neighborhood overlap across the relay graph; clusters echoing internally gain almost nothing. A sybil ring must therefore recruit outside its own knoll of mutual relays, paying real latency and connectivity costs per identity. The persistent fee resembles a relic of older gossip protocols: honest agents keep a ferrous-hard relay position, while each fake node must sustain costly cross-cluster routes.
